data.narrative: Devanshi correctly classified work items by technical risk (Integration, Novelty, Dependency, Scale), front-loaded high-uncertainty risks while respecting hard DAG dependencies, and adapted the delivery plan when external business/legal blockers halted live payment integrations.

dimension_scores.observation: Identified that payments carried both external integration risk and legal merchant account business prerequisites.
dimension_scores.evidence: Separated payment interface contracts from real merchant account preconditions in risk-plan-module-03.md.

dimension_scores.observation: Maintained DAG consistency while reordering by risk; recognized that high-dependency items like Auth must precede risky downstream items.
dimension_scores.evidence: Front-loaded foundational Auth and Listings before spiking payments, preserving valid build ordering.

dimension_scores.observation: Distinguished technical risk from task effort; identified Stripe escrow holds as highest technical risk and concurrency as highest novelty risk.
dimension_scores.evidence: Assigned Risk 5 to Stripe integration, Risk 4 to Availability concurrency, and Risk 1 to Profile CRUD.

dimension_scores.observation: Drafted clear PM escalation notice and explicit interface contract signature for stubbed payments.
dimension_scores.evidence: Specified processPayment signature and two-sentence PM communication in risk-plan-module-03.md.

dimension_scores.observation: Immediately pivoted when client lacked merchant account by stubbing payments and shifting team focus to availability locking.
dimension_scores.evidence: Updated execution plan with WI-07a stub and elevated WI-04 availability without blocking the team.

dimension_scores.observation: Recognized that software boundary contracts isolate teams from third-party operational readiness.
dimension_scores.evidence: Isolated payments behind an interface contract so booking, cancellation, and reviews continue unblocked.

strengths: Clear grasp of risk categories (Integration, Novelty, Dependency, Scale) vs simple task difficulty
Rapid, disciplined adaptation when encountering external non-technical business blockers
Exemplary interface contract definition that isolates downstream features from upstream delays
data.recommendation: Carry this contract-driven isolation technique into vertical slicing and task specification in upcoming packs.

public_evidence.student_action: Classified 13 system work items by risk type and score, front-loaded risk retirement, and adapted execution plan around an external business blocker via an interface stub.
public_evidence.proof: Structured risk matrix, PM escalation communication, and DAG-compliant reordered execution sequence.
public_evidence.ability: Orders software delivery by risk retirement and isolates teams from external business blockers
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows mature engineering judgment to prevent team stalls when third-party or legal dependencies encounter delays.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Ordered build sequence to retire high-uncertainty risks before low-risk CRUD features
Applied time-boxed spike concepts to buy information cheaply before committing architecture
Decoupled blocked payment integration with interface contracts and local stubs

teaching_approaches.detail: Clarified that high-dependency foundational tasks (Auth) differ from high-uncertainty tasks (Stripe)
